title: Deprecated and Removed Features
keywords: legacy php, migration, and professional development
learning_outcomes: Explain what deprecated and removed features contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: recognizing deprecation warnings.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Legacy maintenance preserves real behavior while removing risky assumptions. Use tests to make changes incremental, check the supported PHP/dependency matrix, and migrate deprecated patterns with a documented plan. In this lesson, focus on recognizing deprecation warnings; then compare it with deprecated language behavior. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use deprecated and removed features when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Legacy maintenance preserves real behavior while removing risky assumptions. Use tests to make changes incremental, check the supported PHP/dependency matrix, and migrate deprecated patterns with a documented plan. For deprecated and removed features, begin with recognizing deprecation warnings. Also distinguish deprecated language behavior; removed functions and extensions; migration guides. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
